text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to a survey of trustees of 254 superannuation funds, conducted by research house BIS Shrapnel, some of Australia's best-known funds managers, including BZW Investment Management, County NatWest, National Mutual Funds Management and HSBC Asset Maagement are in danger of losing many of their clients. The survey found that 20 percent of funds expected to replace the managers they used, turning to Maple-Brown Abbott, Rothschild Asset Management, Lend Lease Corporate Services or Mercury Asset Management. Page 1.

The A$2.65 billion takeover of Advance Bank could lead to a confrontation between the Finance Sector Union and St George Bank, with St George refusing to give in to FSU demands that 1,000 planned job cuts be made through voluntary redundancies, with an apeal process. The jobs cuts form a crucial part of St George's plan to extract A$140 million in savings by merging with Advance. Page 1.

Retailing giant Woolworths surprised the market yesterday, posting an 8.6 percent increase in first-half sales to A$8.22 billion. Reflecting a shift from mainstream department store shopping to discount chains, Woolworths' Big W discount department stors posted a 9.5 percent increase in sales to A$1.02 billion. Page 1.

New South Wales Premier Bob Carr, who has refused to comment about Sydney Harbour Casino Holding Ltd's proposal for a lower tax rate on premium players, told Radio National yesterday the only test to the proposal would be the benefit to the state's taxpayers. Page 15.

Wall Street analysts have been left puzzled as to the reasons for Showboat Inc's sale of the Sydney Harbour Casino management company and part of its SHC shareholding to Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting - a deal which resulted in a US$3.50 rise in Showboat's share price to US$23.25. Page 15.

Speculation is mounting that RTZ-CRA is looking to sell its 71 percent stake in Hunter Valley miner Coal & Allied Industries Ltd so it can focus on profitable Indonesian and Queensland mines. Sources say RTZ-CRA would like to secure at least a 15 percent return on its average entry price of A$9.50 a share - valuing Coal & Allied at about A$650 million. Page 17.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Thanks to its focus on food - which accounts for 85 percent of its turnover - and a strong performance by its Big W discount chain, supermarket giant Woolworths Ltd appears to have beaten the slump in the retail sector, yesterday announcing a better-than expected 8.6 percent increase in first-half sales for the 28 weeks to January 5 to A$8.2 billion. Page 19.

Investor enthusiasm for Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting's two-day-old deal to buy management control of Sydney Harbour Casino has boosted the company's market capitalisation by A$200 million - a result that gives PBL a market value of A$3.3 bilion. This means the Packer family has gained an immediate paper profit of A$102 million on its 45 percent holding. Page 19.

Australian financial services giant AMP yesterday announced a major restructuring of its key distribution arm - the first of a series of fundamental reconstructions aimed at putting the group at the forefront of the industry following the Wallis inquiry ito the financial system. Page 19.

In its second submission to the Wallis inquiry into the financial system yesterday, ANZ Bank reiterated its support for the banking industry's opposition to a proposed compulsory insurance scheme for bank depositors, saying prudential supervision should not be aimed at protecting individual institutions from failing. Page 21.

In a warning that confirms fears aired by QNI management at last November's annual meeting that profits for the nickel producer are under severe pressure, the group has cautioned it will return "considerably" lower earnings in the first-half after a sustaned period of falling metal prices and problems with ore supplies. Page 21.

Woodside Petroleum told the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday that data had confirmed the presence of gas in three separate areas at its Keast-1 exploration well on the North West Shelf off Western Australia. Woodside said the well is now being prepared for production testing. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a result described by Woolworths chief executive Reg Clairs as "outstanding", the group achieved an 8.6 percent rise in sales for the first-half of the financial year - in the 28 weeks to January 5, Woolworths sales were A$8.21 billion, compared with $7.56 billion in the previous corresponding period - due largely to a strong supermarket division. Page 29.

St George Bank shares hit a 12-month low of A$7.20 yesterday before finishing at A$7.30, wiping A$160 million - six percent - from the value of its takeover bid for Advance Bank which passed its final legal hurdle yesterday. Page 29.

Following the announcement on Monday of Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting's deal to buy control of Sydney Harbour Casino, stockbroking analysts have upgraded their long-term profit forecasts for the group because of its foray into gambling and investors showed their support by pushing PBL's market value up by A$262 million to A$3.34 billion. Page 29.

Poker machine maker Aristocrat Leisure said yesterday it was confident of reaching prospectus forecasts for the year to June after reappointing its former independent director Frank Burke to try and ease boardroom strife resulting from last year's infighting among the Ainsworth family - the group's major shareholders. Page 31.

West Australian mining entrepreneur Ross Atkins, who was operations manager of WA gold producer St Barbara Mines until he was ousted after a dispute with board member Alan Birchmore, has launched another attempt for control of the group by calling an extrordinary general meeting he hopes will sweep away the existing board. Page 31.

Due to supply problems at its Yabulu nickel refinery in Townsville, reduced metal prices and a stronger Australian dollar, Queensland nickel and cobalt producer QNI, which recently reported a 20 percent decline in annual profit to June, 1996, yesterday jined the growing number of base metals producers to warn of lower first-half profits. Page 31.
THE AGE

Crown Casino chairman Lloyd Williams confirmed yesterday that the Melbourne casino had discussed the possibility of linking some machines and systems with the Sydney Harbour Casino, allowing players in Sydney and Melbourne to play for the same jackpot thrugh external gaming machines linked to a centralised terminal. Page C1.

Claiming that Swiss banks had been "unhelpful and obstructive", the president of the Jewish Community Council of Victoria, Nina Bassat, yesterday called for a boycott of Swiss banks until they release dormant accounts held by Jews before World War II. Whle Swiss banks estimate the disputed funds at A$41 million, other sources suggest the amount owed to Jews could be at least A$700 million. Page C1.

While some retailers have issued profit warnings following their worst Christmas ever, Woolworths yesterday defied the trend, lifting sales in the non-food category by 9.5 percent to A$1.02 billion in the 28 weeks to 5 January. Chief executive officer Rg Clairs said the strong growth in the non-food categories was the result of sales of clothing for adults and children, toys and office supplies. Page C1.

With the Supreme Court yesterday giving its final approval to St George Bank's A$2.65 billion takeover of Advance Bank, the combined bank's management must now face the task of closing 167 branches and up to 1,000 staff. The merger implementation is schedled for 29 January. Page C1.

Women's clothing retailer Cue Designs has been forced to remove returns-policy signs from its stores, after the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission found that Cue was in breach of statutory warranties provided under the Trade Practices Act 1974. Cue was alleged to have misled consumers about their rights to a refund. Page C1.

Because of lower metal prices and disruptions to ore supplies, QNI yesterday warned of considerably lower profits for the December half. Dr Wyn Davies, the managing director of the Queensland nickel and cobalt producer, said the price of nickel since Jul 1996 had averaged US$3.19 a pound, compared with US$3.83 a pound in the previous half-year. Page C2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
